extracted.intended_audience: health insurance issuers, State insurance regulators, actuaries, modelers, and other stakeholders submitting comments on the HHS notice of benefit and payment parameters (risk adjustment, RADV, and rate filing requirements)
extracted.subtask_short: HHS risk adjustment payment notice comments
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and proposed regulatory requirements for the HHS-operated risk adjustment program (model recalibration, RADV error estimation, user fees) and for rate filing justification and CSR loading disclosures for the 2027 benefit year. The page solicits comments on specific proposals and explains methodology and reporting expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequestration application to HHS-operated risk adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: The HHS-operated risk adjustment program is subject to fiscal year 2026 sequestration at a rate of 5.7 percent for payments made from fiscal year 2026 resources; sequestered funds will become available for payment to issuers in the fiscal year following the year in which they are sequestered unless Congress replaces the Joint Committee reductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites OMB Report to Congress and section 256(k)(6) of the BBEDCA; notes Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act extension of the sequestration through FY2031 at 5.7 percent. Implication: payments and budget estimates for the program must account for sequestration timing and rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHS risk adjustment model structure and factors (§153.320)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS risk adjustment models predict plan liability using separate models for adults, children, and infants based on enrollee age, sex, and diagnoses (HCCs), producing a risk score; adult and child models include age-sex, HCCs, interacted HCC count factors, ACFs, RXCs (where applicable), and enrollment duration factors; infant models use 25 mutually exclusive maturity/severity groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists specific factor types (age-sex, HCC, RXC, RXC-HCC interaction, interacted HCC count, affiliated cost factors (ACF), enrollment duration coefficients). Notes historical changes (removal of severity illness factors starting 2023; addition of ACF starting 2026) and that risk scores may be multiplied by CSR adjustment factors. Also notes high-cost risk pool truncation of adult/child/infant models (remove 60% of costs above $1M). Tables 1–6 contain proposed factors; Tables 3,5,6 list HCC selections and infant categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and approach for model recalibration (2027 benefit year)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to recalibrate 2027 HHS risk adjustment models using enrollee-level EDGE data from the 2021, 2022, and 2023 benefit years and to use blended (averaged) coefficients from three separately solved annual models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: promotes stability and gives issuers time to incorporate information for pricing. Costs of services are trended from the data year to the 2027 benefit year. HHS performed data reviews (e.g., for 2023 EDGE data) to identify anomalies and will publish draft coefficients; draft coefficients could change if errors are identified or models modified in response to comments. If final coefficients cannot be finalized in time, HHS will publish them in guidance soon after the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and assessment of model performance statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Each benefit year, HHS examines model R-squared statistics and predictive ratios (PRs) to evaluate model performance; when blending coefficients from separately solved models, HHS will publish R-squared statistics for each model separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R-squared measures percentage of individual variation explained by model (predictive accuracy); PR is weighted mean predicted plan liability divided by weighted mean actual plan liability (PR of 1.0 = perfect prediction). R-squareds and PRs are compared to published estimates for concurrent HHS models; Table 7 shows R-squareds for proposed 2027 models.

rubrics_metrics.name: State payment transfer formula and high-cost risk pool parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Continue to apply the State payment transfer formula as finalized in prior Payment Notices; maintain the high-cost risk pool threshold of $1 million and a 60 percent coinsurance rate for the 2027 benefit year unless changed by notice-and-comment rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No proposed changes to formula or parameters in the rule. Notes prior finalizations (2020 and 2021 Payment Notices) and compatibility with the actuary standards of practice for risk classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation: separate vs combined transfer calculations for catastrophic plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Request for comment on whether to retain separate risk adjustment transfer calculations under the State payment transfer formula for individual catastrophic plans and individual non-catastrophic plans, or to calculate State transfers for these plans together (and in merged-market States possibly with small group plans).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context: 2025 guidance expanded eligibility for catastrophic plans, potentially increasing catastrophic enrollment. HHS is interested in comments about impacts on risk adjustment, market composition, premiums, and State transfers under scenarios (retain separate calculations vs combine) in non-merged and merged market States.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHS Risk Adjustment Data Validation (HHS-RADV) requirements (§§153.350, 153.630)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS will conduct HHS-RADV (IVA followed by SVA) in any State where HHS operates risk adjustment; each issuer must engage an independent IVA entity and provide demographic, enrollment, and medical record documentation for HHS-selected sample enrollees; SVA is performed by an HHS-retained entity to verify IVA findings; HHS then conducts error estimation to calculate an HHS-RADV error rate applied to adjust outlier issuers' PLRSs and State transfers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: ensure issuers provide accurate, high-quality information and that transfers reflect verifiable actuarial risk differences rather than poor-quality data. Process details: sample selection by HHS, IVA by issuer-hired independent entity, SVA by HHS contractor, error estimation based on IVA/SVA findings, adjustments applied to PLRS and transfer calculations for audited benefit year.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHS-RADV error estimation modification (addition of scaling factor αi)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to add an additional scaling factor, αi, to the HHS-RADV error estimation methodology beginning with 2025 benefit year RADV to account for exclusion of enrollees without HCCs from IVA sampling and to ensure HCC-associated error rates apply only to the proportion of an issuer's total PLRS associated with enrollees with HCCs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that current HccPLRSweighti formula (based on sampled enrollees) will be biased when non-HCC enrollees are excluded from the audit sample. αi is constructed using issuer EDGE data: numerator sums mean risk score * BMM across strata 1–9 (enrollees with HCCs); denominator sums across strata 1–10 (all enrollees). Application: TotalERi = HccERi * HccPLRSWeighti * αi; AdjPLRSi = (1 − TotalERi) * PLRSi. Rationale: prevents inappropriately adjusting non-HCC components or double-adjusting demographic/enrollment errors that are adjusted elsewhere. HHS seeks comment on this proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHS risk adjustment user fee methodology and proposed rate (§153.610(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed HHS risk adjustment user fee for 2027 benefit year of $0.20 per member per month (PMPM) to fund HHS operation of the program in States where HHS operates risk adjustment on the State's behalf; fee equals product of monthly billable member months and PMPM user fee as specified in annual notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basis: OMB Circular A-25 policy on user charges for special benefits; methodology: divide projected HHS administrative costs (model/methodology development, collections/payments, account management, data collection, RADV, integrity/audit, analytics, training, operations, personnel) by expected BMM in applicable plans. HHS estimated slightly more than $65 million cost for 2027, similar to 2026. HHS may adjust fee in final rule based on updated enrollment/cost estimates and events that change costs or policies. HHS seeks comment on the proposed fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission requirements for rate filing justification (§154.215) — URRT (Part I)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part I (Unified Rate Review Template, URRT) is required for all single risk pool products (new and existing) and is intended to capture information needed to monitor premium increases and ensure compliance with single risk pool methodology, allowable market-level index adjustments (including risk adjustment payments/charges), and other Federal rating requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: URRT collects plan-level and market-level data, including proposed proposal in 2027 to report CSR amounts and additional revenue from CSR loads in URRT (using most recent annual data available prior to filing year). The URRT-based CSR reporting uses standard methodology set forth in §156.430(c)(2). HHS proposes reporting CSR amounts at plan-level (aggregate) rather than policy-level to reduce burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission requirements for rate filing justification (§154.215) — Consumer Justification Narrative (Part II)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part II is a Written Description Justifying the Rate Increase (consumer-friendly narrative) required only for rate increases in single risk pool products that are subject to review (a plan with a rate increase of 15 percent or greater).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part II should provide justification for the rate increase, describe relevant Part I data, the assumptions used to develop the rate increase, and explain the most significant factors causing the rate increase in consumer-friendly terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission requirements for rate filing justification (§154.215) — Actuarial memorandum (Part III)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Part III actuarial memorandum is required for any rate increase in a single risk pool plan, for any filing containing QHPs or when a State requires it, and for all plans in States without an Effective Rate Review Program for which CMS reviews the filing; it must include actuarial reasoning, assumptions, justifications, methodologies supporting URRT entries, and appropriate actuarial certifications for index rate development and plan-specific premium development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuer must explain how plan-specific modifiers are developed and applied to market-wide adjusted index rate to derive plan-adjusted index rate. For CSR loading, the actuarial memorandum must: specify actual CSRs paid for a recent plan year (if available), specify CSR load factor and explain its determination, and explain how additional revenue from CSR load compares to expected CSR amounts. If precise CSR actuals are not available by filing deadline, CMS will accept a reasonable estimate and methodology in the actuarial memorandum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements and expectations for CSR load reporting and actuarial justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Issuers that make plan-level adjustments to account for unreimbursed CSRs (CSR loading) must report CSR amounts paid on behalf of enrollees, the CSR load factor for each plan, the additional revenue expected from the CSR load, and the expected amount of CSRs to be paid for the upcoming plan year in the URRT and actuarial memorandum; issuers must explain methodology and compare amounts to demonstrate actuarial justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed continuing requirement starting with 2027 plan year filings; reporting uses most recent annual data available prior to filing (typically two years prior). Purpose: enable State/CMS to determine whether load factor is actuarially justified and not excessive in relation to expected unreimbursed CSRs. HHS states an 'actuarially justified CSR load factor' is one calibrated on actual experience and that only accounts for projected revenue loss without materially exceeding it. CMS expects States with Effective Rate Review Programs to determine actuarial justification; HHS may review in other States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of CMS standard methodology to calculate CSR amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS standard methodology requires re-adjudicating the complete set of claims incurred by an enrollee in the CSR plan variation as if they had been enrolled in associated standard plan to determine the difference in out-of-pocket costs (deductibles, copays, coinsurance) which equals the CSR amount provided by issuer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS believes the standard methodology is most accurate and familiar to issuers (it was required for 2017 when CMS provided advance CSR payments). For URRT reporting, CMS proposes issuers use the standard methodology to calculate aggregate plan-level CSR amounts but does not propose requiring submission via the CSR reconciliation process (policy-level electronic submissions) to reduce burden. If precise PY data are not available by rate filing deadline, a reasonable estimate with explanation in actuarial memorandum is acceptable.
